conflict_topics: Strong-smelling cooking (sambal belacan) affecting shared spaces
Timing of cooking relative to A's video calls
Laundry in service yard absorbing smells
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents negotiated with concrete, practical proposals (scheduling by nights, opening window, closing doors) rather than abstract principles.
Key acceptance lines made settlements explicit: D 'after 7 p.m. works' (Turn17); C 'Yes, that works.' (Turn21); B 'Yes, if I close my door, that works.' (Turn26).
Minor redundancy: D repeats the settlement statement twice at the end (Turns 27 and 31).
evaluation.final_reason: Parties agreed concrete accommodations: D accepted cooking after 7 p.m. and on specific nights (D: 'Okay, after 7 p.m. works for me.' Turn17; D: 'So, after 7 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays? That works for me.' Turn20), C accepted that schedule ('Yes, that works.' Turn21), and D offered to open the kitchen window while cooking while B agreed to close their bedroom door ('I can open the kitchen window when I cook.' Turn25; 'Yes, if I close my door, that works.' Turn26). These mutual, explicit acceptances settled the outstanding incompatible demands.
position_change_notes: Agent D: initially resisted limitations ('It's a kitchen. We all cook.' Turn4) but then accepted constraints—timing (after 7 p.m., and Tue/Thu) and a physical mitigation (open window) (Turns17,20,25).
Agent B: initially complained about room smell but accepted the practical mitigation of closing their door when D cooks ('Yes, if I close my door, that works.' Turn26).
Agent C: proposed a schedule to protect laundry (Mon/Wed/Fri) (Turn11) but accepted D's counterproposal for Tue/Thu ('Yes, that works.' Turn21), showing flexibility.

Agent A: maintained the original request for no strong-smelling cooking during call times and accepted the after-7pm arrangement (Turn16); A's position did not reverse but was accommodated by others' concessions.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A asks that nobody cook strong-smelling food in the flat; Agent B supports that the smell reaches his room (Turn1-2). A clear substantive demand is made but no acceptance yet.

Agent D pushes back: 'Okay, I hear you about the smell. But it's a kitchen. We all cook. Your food has smells too.' (Turn4). This directly resists A's request and frames the kitchen as shared, increasing conflict.

A narrows the complaint to 'very strong' smells; D challenges the definition and points to curries: 'What is a "very strong" smell? Your curries have strong smells too.' (Turn5-6). The substantive disagreement about which smells should be restricted continues.

A explains difference of sambal smell; B proposes a mitigation: 'What if we all just agree to close our bedroom doors when we're cooking something strong?' (Turn7-8). A practical proposal appears, softening the dispute though not resolving it.

C points out bedroom-door proposal doesn't address laundry in the service yard: 'That doesn't help the laundry in the service yard.' (Turn9). B agrees (Turn10). The issue broadens (multiple incompatible interests), making resolution harder.

C proposes specific laundry days: 'I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings. Could you cook it on the other nights?' (Turn11). A replies the timing doesn't help their calls (Turn12). The schedule clash remains unresolved.

D expresses concern about being heavily restricted: 'So I can't cook on any weekday evening at all? It's a shared kitchen.' (Turn15). A responds with concrete alternatives: '...after 7 p.m. Could you do it after that, or on Saturday?' (Turn16). Positions sharpen over allowable times.
D concedes a timing constraint: 'Okay, after 7 p.m. works for me.' (Turn17). This reduces the direct conflict with A, but B and C's problems (room/laundry) remain.

Negotiation over concrete nights: C asks about their Mon/Wed/Fri proposal (Turn19); D offers 'after 7 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays' (Turn20). Parties are narrowing options, reducing but not eliminating disagreement.
C accepts D's proposed nights ('Yes, that works.' Turn21), but B reiterates the smell will still affect their room regardless of schedule (Turn23). B's concern remains unresolved.

D offers a physical mitigation: 'I can open the kitchen window when I cook.' (Turn25). B accepts: 'Yes, if I close my door, that works.' (Turn26). This directly resolves B's room concern; only a minor remaining issue (service-yard laundry was already accommodated by schedule changes) is left to confirm.
Agent D affirms settlement: 'Okay, good. So that's settled then.' (Turn27 and repeated Turn31). By this point all parties have accepted concrete arrangements (timing and window/door mitigation).

substantive_insights: Conflict arose from differing effects of smells: video-call interference, laundry contamination, and room intrusion require different mitigations.
Resolution combined time-based scheduling (to avoid clashes with laundry and calls) and physical mitigation (open window / close door), showing plural solutions for multi-issue conflicts.

Participants were willing to trade small inconveniences (D limiting cooking nights/times; B closing door) rather than spend money or change the kitchen, which aligns with the opening constraint that no one wants to pay for fixes.

normalizations: Adjusted resolution_round from 11 to 12 to match the conflict trajectory.
